clue.text: Chief Constable carries it on a beat

indicators.note: the constable carries, or holds within him, the reworked letters

parts.note: PC, police constable

indicators.note: beat means batter or pound, so these three little words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A senior police officer walking the streets on patrol, carrying something.
explanation.walkthrough: A constable's 'beat' looks like his patrol route, but here 'beat' signals the anagram; 'carries' puts the result inside the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontiac was an Odawa war leader of the 1760s, so a Native American chief.

clue.text: Harry and Kitty embracing for all to see

indicators.note: the kitty hugs, or holds within it, the film-rating letter

parts.note: a kitty is a pooled fund of money, a purse
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Two people, or a man and a cat, cuddling in public.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to chase and hound them relentlessly, a close synonym.

clue.text: Handy piece of underwear and thing holding it up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the assembled letters are read from bottom to top
the 'thing' holds 'it', the underwear just mentioned, within itself

parts.note: to have a thing for something is to have a yen, a craving
a bra

explanation.surface: A useful garment and the support that keeps it in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handy is close at hand, conveniently within reach.

clue.text: Crawl home with good swine I feasted on

parts.note: at home is IN
a swine, a contemptible person, is a rat
ate

explanation.surface: Someone crawling home after gorging on a fine pig.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl to someone is to fawn and toady, seeking favour obsequiously.

clue.text: A privilege to carry Bill's make-up

indicators.note: the privilege holds, or carries, the bill inside it

parts.note: a charter is a granted privilege or right
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A right that lets someone bring along Bill's cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: One's make-up is one's nature or personality, the qualities that form a person.

clue.text: Picket almost destroyed delivery van

parts.note: a picket is a stake or post

indicators.note: almost means one letter short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: bust, broken

explanation.surface: A strike picket nearly wrecks a delivery vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbus is a rural British mail van that also carries passengers.

clue.text: Cycle in traffic, I'd say

indicators.note: the setter is saying the word out loud, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: to traffic in goods is to peddle them

explanation.surface: A cyclist out in busy traffic, offering an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To cycle is to ride a bike by working its foot levers, so a verb synonym.

clue.text: Erection to blame for this headache?

definitions.text: Erection to blame for this headache?

parts.words: Erection to blame for this headache?
parts.note: an erection is a structure put up, and an office block with poor air can cause headaches among its workers

explanation.surface: A smutty question about what caused someone's headache.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition names illness, such as headaches, blamed on an unhealthy office environment.

clue.text: See 6
See 6
Stand to relieve back pressure?

definitions.meaning: a defensive fight made while retreating, a last stand
playfully, something done by the guard at the back to ease pressure there

explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard defends a retreating army from behind, so its fight is a defensive stand.

clue.text: The best book has rotten cover

indicators.note: the rotten word has the book within it
the rotten word forms a cover wrapped around the book

parts.note: rotten food is uneatable

explanation.surface: A top-ranked book with a decaying jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever cannot be beaten is supreme, the very finest.

clue.text: A challenge to drop last part of Jewish calendar

indicators.note: the challenge word loses its final letter

parts.note: a dare

explanation.surface: A dare to skip the final section of the Jewish year.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar is a month of the Hebrew year, falling around February and March.

clue.text: Cheap fleece? Darn parts to take out

indicators.note: the two words split apart the date-going word, sitting in its middle

parts.note: to take someone out is to see them, as in dating
to fleece someone is to con them
darn and drat are both mild curses

explanation.surface: A shoddy fleece garment: mend parts of it, then remove them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheap and shoddy is of inferior quality, not first-class.

clue.text: Badly run regiment's rule-breaking

indicators.note: badly run suggests letters handled wrongly and set out in a muddle

explanation.surface: A poorly managed army unit is breaking the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: An interregnum is a gap between reigns, a break in the rule of a monarch.

clue.text: Red tissue breaking bones up again

definitions.note: to bone up is to study hard, here a second time

indicators.note: breaking means split up and broken apart, so the letters reassemble

explanation.surface: Inflamed tissue as bones fracture, a medical scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To bone up is to swot, so someone doing it again goes over the material afresh.

clue.text: A simple task to keep lake and river sparkling

indicators.note: the simple task keeps, or holds, the lake's letter inside

parts.note: a gimme is an easy thing, from golf's short putt conceded
L, abbreviation for lake
R, abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An easy job of keeping lake and river shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gleaming faintly with flickering light is shining softly, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Specific books let me think I'm a handyman

parts.note: a specific is a detail, a fact
OT, the Old Testament books
um is the noise of someone pausing to think

explanation.surface: Someone musing that they are a handyman because of particular books.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a general servant who does all kinds of odd jobs.

clue.text: Give Israeli man small Flash video game

parts.note: to grant is to give
Uri is a common Israeli male name
S, abbreviation for small
a mo, moment, is a flash of time

explanation.surface: Handing a small Israeli man a Flash-based video game.
explanation.definitionFit: Gran Turismo is a long-running PlayStation car-racing series.

clue.text: Places for the rest of the lecturers

definitions.text: Places for the rest of the lecturers

parts.words: Places for the rest of the lecturers
parts.note: read as lounges where university staff take their rest, while seeming to mean the remaining lecturers

explanation.surface: Seating arrangements for the lecturers not yet placed.
explanation.definitionFit: These are staff lounges for fellows at Oxford and Cambridge colleges, where dons relax.

clue.text: See 18
A fan of peppermint oil extract?

indicators.note: an extract is a piece taken out of the words

explanation.surface: Someone who loves peppermint oil essence.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen on something is colloquially being 'into' it, as in into jazz.

clue.text: Fresh start before love is turned to dust?

indicators.note: the dusty word comes first, ahead of the love word

parts.note: ground, reduced to powder
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A new beginning before romance crumbles away.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back to the starting point means beginning again from scratch.

clue.text: See 18
In France you will carry off unfinished food

indicators.note: the French word will carry, or hold, the shortened word inside it

parts.note: tu is French for you

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: In France, you will take away the uneaten food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd, a staple food made from soya milk.

clue.text: Nepotist involved with immoral city concepts

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A corrupt official mixed up with immoral urban ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes the ideas and attitudes typical of a big urban centre.

clue.text: Strange for us to produce a best-selling album

parts.note: rum means odd or strange
something for us is ours

explanation.surface: It is odd that we made a hit record.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumours is the 1977 Fleetwood Mac LP, one of the top-selling records ever.

clue.text: Don opens wrong institute

indicators.note: the don word opens up the wrong word and sits inside it

parts.note: a wrong is a sin
to don clothes is to wear them

explanation.surface: A university don launches an institute by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone formally in an office by oath is to induct or institute them.
